beats.caption: A design win is a socket picked before the product exists
beats.text: Chip designers choose suppliers years before a product ships. Each slot on a board is a socket, and whoever gets picked for it is the design win. Nothing is sold yet.

beats.caption: The supplier's chip is designed into the board
beats.text: Once a customer picks a part for a product still in design, the supplier has a seat at the table. The part gets qualified, the board is laid out around it, and the customer is slow to change it.

beats.caption: Revenue follows one to three years later
beats.text: The product reaches volume production after a long development cycle, and revenue ramps with it. Companies cite design wins to show future revenue long before it appears in results.

beats.caption: Losing the socket at the next generation drops the stream
beats.text: When the next product generation comes, the socket can go to a rival. The revenue stream stops in one step, so a single lost design can outweigh a year of ordinary sales.

beats.caption: Read design wins as a lead on future revenue
beats.text: A design win is a lead, not a sale. Its value depends on how many sockets a supplier holds and how sticky they are. Related: Marvell (MRVL), Broadcom (AVGO), Astera Labs (ALAB), Credo (CRDO), Lattice (LSCC).
